title: Technologies & Threads Through the Fabric of Our Lives

reader_summary.headline: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6&Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6&Z podcast. I'm Sonal Choxi and as your primary host, editor and showrunner here of the past seven years. I wanted to share some favorite episodes selected for you, not just by me, but by you as they were very popular among listeners, too.

key_points.text: The third of these three special rerun episodes is a conversation that originally took place in October 2020 in the midst of the pandemic.
key_points.evidence_quote: The third of these three special rerun episodes is a conversation that originally took place in October 2020 in the midst of the pandemic, hence some initial sound issues, but they quickly get resolved, so make sure to hang on.

key_points.text: And it's probably my personal single most favorite episode, which is a really hard thing to say after overseeing nearly what, 700 plus episodes.
key_points.evidence_quote: And it's probably my personal single most favorite episode, which is a really hard thing to say after overseeing nearly what, 700 plus episodes.

key_points.text: But for me, it perfectly captures how I think of the signature identity of this show and my work.
key_points.evidence_quote: But for me, it perfectly captures how I think of the signature identity of this show and my work, which is at the intersection of technology and humanity.

thesis: The episode discusses Virginia Postrel's book 'The Fabric of Civilization,' which explores the central role of textiles in the history of technology, science, commerce, and civilization. The conversation covers topics ranging from the genetics of cotton and the supply chain of silk to the storage of knowledge and the meta-narrative of how innovation happens.
